literal: From the head fallen hair like-they people, from standing fallen when.
translation: When people fall from their honorable standing, they are like hair that has fallen from the head.
modern: மக்கள் தம் உயர்ந்த நிலையிலிருந்து தாழ்ந்தால், அவர்கள் தலையிலிருந்து உதிர்ந்த மயிரைப் போன்றவர்கள் ஆவார்கள்.
explanation: This couplet uses a striking simile to explain the loss of honor. Hair is carefully groomed and valued as long as it remains on the head, but becomes worthless dirt the moment it falls. Similarly, people are respected when they maintain their dignity and moral standing, but lose all their worth when they fall from that honorable state.
